brief: UBS sales desk note ahead of Tuesday's October CPI, the last reading before the Fed's Dec 8-9 meeting. Waller said he would back a 25bp December hike even if inflation improves, but a 50bp hike should be considered if core CPI rises 0.3% or more m/m. UBS forecasts headline CPI at 0.26% m/m, below 0.29% consensus and 0.32% UBS Nowcast, and core at 0.23%, versus 0.24% consensus, implying the 50bp threshold likely goes unmet. Nvidia fell 5.5% Monday on Jensen Huang allegations; the desk's best estimate concentrates China exposure in Singapore revenue and says investors are not backing away from a roughly $135bn January-quarter revenue bogey. Brent fell below $90 for the first time since August, down about 23% from its $118 high, as Trump said he would hold off new Iran strikes and OPEC output rose; Iran rejected US talk of negotiations and reasserted its Hormuz conditions, leaving no clear path to normal flows. Separately, Keirstead argues the market has turned too bearish on AI data-center political risk since midterm-driven permitting fights target mainly 2028-plus capacity, while Arcuri estimates SOX pricing already implies a 30-35% EPS cut and about 55GW of 2028 shipments against 50GW of high-confidence powered-shell capacity.
